# Sloc Cloc and Code (scc)

![SCC illustration](./scc.jpg)

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. In short one tool to rule them all.

Also it has a very short name which is easy to type `scc`.

If you don't like sloc cloc and code feel free to use the name `Succinct Code Counter`.

Licensed under MIT licence.

## Install

### Snap

A snap install exists.

`$ sudo snap install scc`

*NB* Snap installed applications cannot run outside of `/home` so you may encounter issues if you use snap and attempt to run outside this directory.

### Homebrew

Or if you have Homebrew installed

`$ brew install scc`

### Fedora

Fedora Linux users can use a COPR repository:

`$ sudo dnf copr enable lihaohong/scc && sudo dnf install scc`

### MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts

`$ sudo port install scc`

### Scoop

Or if you are using Scoop on Windows

`$ scoop install scc`

### Chocolatey

Or if you are using Chocolatey on Windows

`$ choco install scc`

### WinGet

Or if you are using WinGet on Windows

`winget install --id benboyter.scc --source winget`

### FreeBSD

On FreeBSD, scc is available as a package

`$ pkg install scc`

Or, if you prefer to build from source, you can use the ports tree

`$ cd /usr/ports/devel/scc && make install clean`

### Run in Docker

Go to the directory you want to run scc from.

Run the command below to run the latest release of scc on your current working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/pwd"  ghcr.io/boyter/scc:master scc /pwd
```

### Manual

Binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux and macOS for both i386 and x86_64 machines are available from the releases page.

## Usage

Command line usage of `scc` is designed to be as simple as possible.
Full details can be found in `scc --help` or `scc -h`.

```text
Sloc, Cloc and Code. Count lines of code in a directory with complexity estimation.

Usage:
  scc [flags] [files or directories]

Flags:
      --avg-wage int                       average wage value used for basic COCOMO calculation (default 56286)
      --binary                             disable binary file detection
      --by-file                            display output for every file
  -m, --character                          calculate max and mean characters per line
      --ci                                 enable CI output settings where stdout is ASCII
      --cocomo-project-type string         change COCOMO model type [organic, semi-detached, embedded, "custom,1,1,1,1"] (default "organic")
      --count-as string                    count extension as language [e.g. jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" maps extension jsp to html and chead to C Header]
      --count-ignore                       set to allow .gitignore and .ignore files to be counted
      --currency-symbol string             set currency symbol (default "$")
      --debug                              enable debug output
      --directory-walker-job-workers int   controls the maximum number of workers which will walk the directory tree (default 8)
  -a, --dryness                            calculate the DRYness of the project (implies --uloc)
      --eaf float                          the effort adjustment factor derived from the cost drivers (1.0 if rated nominal) (default 1)
      --exclude-dir strings                directories to exclude (default [.git,.hg,.svn])
  -x, --exclude-ext strings                ignore file extensions (overrides include-ext) [comma separated list: e.g. go,java,js]

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

You can customize COCOMO calculation with:

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")
- `--eaf` - Effort adjustment factor (default 1.0)
- `--currency-symbol` - Set currency symbol (default "$")

## LOCOMO

LOCOMO is an extension of COCOMO for calculating costs when using LLM (Large Language Model) based development approaches. It estimates token counts, API costs, and developer time when using AI assistants.

This is an experimental feature for estimating costs when using AI-powered development tools.

## Output Formats

scc supports multiple output formats for integration with other tools:

- `tabular` (default) - Human-readable table format
- `wide` - Wider table with additional statistics
- `json` - JSON format for programmatic processing
- `json2` - Alternative JSON format
- `csv` - CSV format
- `csv-stream` - Streaming CSV format
- `cloc-yaml` - YAML format compatible with cloc
- `html` - HTML report
- `html-table` - HTML table only
- `sql` - SQL CREATE and INSERT statements
- `sql-insert` - SQL INSERT statements only
- `openmetrics` - OpenMetrics/Prometheus format

Example:

```bash
scc --format json .
scc --format csv --output report.csv .
```

## Ignore Files

`scc` supports .ignore files inside directories that it scans. This is similar to how ripgrep, ag and tokei work. .ignore files are 100% the same as .gitignore files with the same syntax, and as such `scc` will ignore files and directories listed in them. You can add .ignore files to ignore things like vendored dependency checked in files.

By default scc will also respect .gitignore files.

## Large File Detection

scc can identify and optionally exclude large files from counting to focus on code that matters.

Use `--large-line-count` and `--large-byte-count` to set thresholds, and `--no-large` to exclude them from output.

## Minified/Generated File Detection

scc can identify minified and generated files and optionally exclude them from counts.

- `--min` - Identify minified files
- `--gen` - Identify generated files
- `--no-min` - Exclude minified files from output
- `--no-gen` - Exclude generated files from output
- `--no-min-gen` - Exclude both minified and generated files

## Remapping

You can remap file extensions to different languages using the `--count-as` flag:

```bash
scc --count-as jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" .
```

This maps `.jsp` files to HTML and `.chead` files to C Header.

You can also remap based on file content:

- `--remap-unknown` - Check unknown file types for a string and remap
- `--remap-all` - Check all files for a string and remap

Example:

```bash
scc --remap-unknown "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header" .
```

## Badges

You can generate badges for your repository showing lines of code counts.

The service at `https://sloc.xyz/` provides badges for GitHub repositories.

Example badge URL:
```
https://sloc.xyz/github/boyter/scc/
```

## Features

`scc` includes many features to help you count code accurately:

- Very fast and gets faster the more CPU you throw at it
- Accurate
- Works very well across multiple platforms without slowdown (Windows, Linux, macOS)
- Large language support
- Can ignore duplicate files
- Has complexity estimations
- You need to tell the difference between Coq and Verilog in the same directory
- cloc yaml output support so potentially a drop in replacement for some users
- Can identify or ignore minified files
- Able to identify many #! files
- Can ignore large files by lines or bytes
- Can calculate the ULOC or unique lines of code by file, language or project
- Supports multiple output formats for integration, CSV, SQL, JSON, HTML and more

## Complexity Estimates

Complexity estimates are provided for supported languages. The complexity estimate is an approximation similar to cyclomatic complexity. The intent is not to be perfect but provide a good enough indication of complexity.

Example output with complexity enabled:

```text
$ scc --complexity
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076
```

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

To calculate DRYness percentage use the `--dryness` flag or `-a`:

```text
$ scc --dryness .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")

import subprocess, os, tempfile, json, re, shutil

def run(*a):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+list(a), capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode

# Load langs
with open("/tmp/langs.txt") as f:
    lines=f.read().strip().split("\n")
lang_ext={}
for l in lines:
    m=re.match(r"^(.*) \((.*)\)$", l)
    name=m.group(1)
    exts=[e.strip() for e in m.group(2).split(",") if e.strip()!=""]
    lang_ext[name]=exts

fname_map=json.load(open("/tmp/fname_map.json"))

# Candidates for line comments
line_tokens = ["//", "#", "--", "%", ";", "!", "'", "\"", "*", "/", ">", "?", ":", "|", ".", "..", "++", "%%", ";;", "!!", "--", "REM", "rem", "❯", "⍝", "⍝⍝", "//", "/*", "<!--", "(*", "{", "/*", "##", "@", "$", ":", "C ", "c ", "*", "!", "D ", "d "]
# Deduplicate and keep order
seen=set()
line_tokens2=[]
for t in line_tokens:
    if t not in seen:
        seen.add(t)
        line_tokens2.append(t)
line_tokens=line_tokens2
print("tokens",line_tokens)

# For each lang, batch test
results={}
for lang, exts in lang_ext.items():
    if lang.startswith("CloudFormation"):
        continue
    fentry=fname_map.get(lang)
    if fentry is None:
        continue
    # parse fentry
    extra=[]
    prefix=""
    if isinstance(fentry, list):
        if len(fentry)==2 and isinstance(fentry[1], list):
            fname=fentry[0]
            extra=fentry[1]
        elif len(fentry)==3:
            fname=fentry[0]
            prefix=fentry[2]
        else:
            fname=fentry[0]
    else:
        fname=fentry
    # Determine extension for batch: if fname starts with "a.", use that ext, else need separate dirs (skip batch for now)
    if not fname.startswith("a."):
        print(f"skip batch for {lang} fname {fname}")
        continue
    # ext is after "a."
    ext=fname[2:]  # e.g., "go", "heex", "d.ts" (for TypeScript Typings, ext is "d.ts", fname "a.d.ts")
    # Create temp dir with one file per token
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    # Map sanitized token to filename
    token_to_file={}
    for idx, tok in enumerate(line_tokens):
        # filename must be unique and valid: use idx
        test_fname=f"t{idx}.{ext}"
        content=prefix+tok+" test\n" if prefix else tok+" test\n"
        # For tokens that are empty? skip
        open(os.path.join(d,test_fname),"w").write(content)
        token_to_file[test_fname]=tok
    # Run scc
    o=run(*(extra+["--by-file","--format","json",d]))[0].strip()
    if o=="[]" or o=="":
        print(f"{lang} no results")
        shutil.rmtree(d)
        continue
    try:
        j=json.loads(o)
    except:
        print(f"{lang} json err {o[:200]}")
        shutil.rmtree(d)
        continue
    # j is list of language summaries, each with Files
    # Collect per-file
    file_results={}
    for summ in j:
        for f in summ.get("Files",[]):
            fn=f["Filename"]
            file_results[fn]=(f["Code"],f["Comment"],f["Blank"],summ["Name"])
    # For each token, check
    lang_res={}
    for test_fname, tok in token_to_file.items():
        if test_fname not in file_results:
            # file not counted? maybe ignored? e.g., .gitignore?
            lang_res[tok]="N/A"
        else:
            code,com,blank,name=file_results[test_fname]
            # If prefix exists, then total lines 2: prefix code + test line. If test is comment, com=1, code=1. If test is code, code=2.
            # If no prefix, lines 1: com=1 => comment, code=1 => code
            if prefix:
                if com==1 and code==1:
                    lang_res[tok]="comment"
                elif code==2:
                    lang_res[tok]="code"
                else:
                    lang_res[tok]=f"code{code}com{com}"
            else:
                if com==1:
                    lang_res[tok]="comment"
                elif code==1:
                    lang_res[tok]="code"
                else:
                    lang_res[tok]=f"code{code}com{com}"
    results[lang]=lang_res
    # Print only comments
    comments=[t for t,v in lang_res.items() if v=="comment"]
    print(f"{lang}: {comments}")
    shutil.rmtree(d)

with open("/tmp/line_results.json","w") as out:
    json.dump(results,out,indent=2)

import subprocess, os, tempfile, json, re, shutil
def run(*a):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+list(a), capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode
with open("/tmp/langs.txt") as f:
    lines=f.read().strip().split("\n")
lang_ext={}
for l in lines:
    m=re.match(r"^(.*) \((.*)\)$", l)
    lang_ext[m.group(1)]=[e.strip() for e in m.group(2).split(",") if e.strip()!=""]
fname_map=json.load(open("/tmp/fname_map.json"))
# candidates: words + operators
words = ["if","else","elif","elsif","for","while","until","switch","case","select","try","catch","except","finally","with","and","or","match","loop","foreach","do","func","function","def","class","go","defer","fallthrough","return","break","continue","goto","in","is","not","then","fi","done","when","where","unless","elsunless","given","default","redo","retry","rescue","ensure","raise","assert","lambda","yield","async","await","import","package","var","const","type","struct","interface","enum"]
ops = ["&&","||","==","!=","??"]
cands = words+ops
results={}
for lang, exts in lang_ext.items():
    if lang.startswith("CloudFormation"):
        continue
    fentry=fname_map.get(lang)
    if fentry is None:
        continue
    extra=[]
    prefix=""
    if isinstance(fentry, list):
        if len(fentry)==2 and isinstance(fentry[1], list):
            fname=fentry[0]; extra=fentry[1]
        elif len(fentry)==3:
            fname=fentry[0]; prefix=fentry[2]
        else:
            fname=fentry[0]
    else:
        fname=fentry
    if not fname.startswith("a."):
        # skip filename-only for now, handle separately
        continue
    ext=fname[2:]
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    cand_to_file={}
    for idx, kw in enumerate(cands):
        test_fname=f"c{idx}.{ext}"
        # content: "x kw y\n" with prefix if needed
        # For prefix langs (Objective C, V), need prefix + "x kw y\n"
        # But need to ensure prefix doesn't add complexity itself? Prefix "fn main() {}\n" has no complexity? Check: "fn main() {}\n" for V: does it have complexity? Likely 0. Good. "@interface X\n" for Objective C: 0. Good.
        content=prefix+f"x {kw} y\n" if prefix else f"x {kw} y\n"
        open(os.path.join(d,test_fname),"w").write(content)
        cand_to_file[test_fname]=kw
    o=run(*(extra+["--by-file","--format","json",d]))[0].strip()
    if o=="[]" or o=="":
        shutil.rmtree(d); continue
    try:
        j=json.loads(o)
    except:
        shutil.rmtree(d); continue
    file_results={}
    for summ in j:
        for f in summ.get("Files",[]):
            # Only consider files that match expected lang? For ambiguous, need to filter by language? For MATLAB/Objective C, files may misclassify. Check f["Language"]?
            file_results[f["Filename"]]=(f["Complexity"],summ["Name"],f["Language"])
    lang_res=[]
    for fn, kw in cand_to_file.items():
        if fn not in file_results:
            continue
        cx, summ_name, file_lang=file_results[fn]
        # If file_lang != lang (misclassified due to ambiguous), skip? For MATLAB/Objective C, need to handle.
        # For now, only count if file_lang == lang (or summ_name == lang?)
        # For random langs (HEEx etc.), file_lang may differ randomly, so skip those? But then results unreliable.
        # For deterministic, file_lang should == lang. For random, it may differ, but we still want to record? For HEEx, complexity? HEEx likely 0 for all, Phoenix also? Let's just record if cx>0 regardless of lang? But need to attribute to correct lang.
        # Better: if file_lang != lang, then this test file was misclassified, so ignore (don't record for this lang).
        if file_lang != lang:
            # For random langs, this will happen often. Skip.
            continue
        # For prefix langs, need to subtract prefix complexity? Prefix alone has 0, so cx>0 means kw adds.
        # But need baseline: what is cx for "x y\n" without kw? Should be 0. So cx>0 means kw counted.
        if cx>0:
            lang_res.append(kw)
    results[lang]=lang_res
    print(f"{lang}: {lang_res}")
    shutil.rmtree(d)
with open("/tmp/cx_results.json","w") as out:
    json.dump(results,out,indent=2)

with open("/tmp/langs.txt") as f:
    lines=f.read().strip().split("\n")
lang_ext={}
for l in lines:
    m=re.match(r"^(.*) \((.*)\)$", l)
    lang_ext[m.group(1)]=[e.strip() for e in m.group(2).split(",") if e.strip()!=""]

# Build ext map deterministically
# For each ext (lower), list langs
from collections import defaultdict
ext_langs=defaultdict(list)
for lang, exts in lang_ext.items():
    for e in exts:
        ext_langs[e.lower()].append(lang)

# Deterministic choices for ambiguous
choices={
    "json": "JSON",
    "yaml": "YAML",
    "yml": "YAML",
    "m": "MATLAB",  # default, with heuristic for Objective C
    "v": "Coq",  # default, with heuristic
    "tex": "TeX",  # pick TeX (vs LaTeX)
    "tt": "TemplateToolkit",  # vs Treetop
    "heex": "HEEx",  # vs Phoenix
    "dockerfile": "Dockerfile",
    "makefile": "Makefile",
    "gvimrc": "Vim Script",
    "vimrc": "Vim Script",
}
ext_map={}
for ext, langs in ext_langs.items():
    if len(langs)==1:
        ext_map[ext]=langs[0]
    else:
        # ambiguous
        if ext in choices:
            ext_map[ext]=choices[ext]
        else:
            # duplicates same lang? e.g., dockerfile ['Dockerfile','Dockerfile'] -> same
            if len(set(langs))==1:
                ext_map[ext]=langs[0]
            else:
                print(f"ambiguous no choice {ext} {langs}")
                ext_map[ext]=langs[0]

# Check filename vs extension: for exts that are filenames (like "makefile", "dockerfile", "gemfile", etc.), they should match both extension and filename?
# Our ext_map currently maps extension "makefile" -> Makefile. For file "Makefile" (no dot), extension logic (after dot) wouldn't match. Need filename map.

def parse_bool(s):
    # Go strconv.ParseBool accepts: 1,t,T,TRUE,true,True,0,f,F,FALSE,false,False
    if s in ("1", "t", "T", "TRUE", "true", "True"):
        return True, None
    if s in ("0", "f", "F", "FALSE", "false", "False"):
        return False, None
    return None, f'strconv.ParseBool: parsing "{s}": invalid syntax'

def parse_int(s):
    try:
        # Go ParseInt allows leading +/-, base 0? For simplicity, base 10
        # Also handles underscores? Ignore.
        v = int(s, 10)
        return v, None
    except:
        return None, f'strconv.ParseInt: parsing "{s}": invalid syntax'

def parse_float(s):
    try:
        v = float(s)
        return v, None
    except:
        return None, f'strconv.ParseFloat: parsing "{s}": invalid syntax'

def flag_error(msg):
    # Returns error string to print to stderr (Error: ... + Usage + Flags)
    return f"Error: {msg}\nUsage:\n  scc [flags] [files or directories]\n\nFlags:\n" + flags_help_block()

def flags_help_block():
    # Extract flags block from HELP_TEXT (after "Flags:\n")
    # HELP_TEXT starts with "Sloc...\nVersion...\n...\nUsage:\n  scc...\n\nFlags:\n      --avg-wage..."
    # We want just the flags part (from "      --avg-wage" onwards)
    idx = HELP_TEXT.find("Flags:\n")
    if idx >= 0:
        return HELP_TEXT[idx+len("Flags:\n"):]

# Complete tabular formatting (override previous incomplete)
def format_tabular_v2(lang_stats_sorted, total, opts, total_bytes, total_uloc, elapsed=0.001):
    ci = opts["ci"]
    no_hborder = opts["no-hborder"]
    no_complexity = opts["no-complexity"]

    do_uloc = opts.get("uloc", False) or opts.get("dryness", False)

    do_percent = opts.get("percent", False)
    if ci:
        hborder = "-" * 79
        inner_hyphen = "-" * 79
    else:
        hborder = "─" * 79
        inner_hyphen = "-" * 79
    lines_out = []
    def add_border():
        if not no_hborder:
            lines_out.append(hborder)

    import sys
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    opts, positionals, err = parse_args(argv)
    if err:
        sys.stderr.write(flag_error(err) + "\n")
        sys.exit(1)

import subprocess, os, tempfile
def run_orig(*a):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+list(a), capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode
def run_new(*a):
    r=subprocess.run(["python3","scc.py"]+list(a), capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode
def test(name, setup, args=[], setup_fn=None):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    for fname, content in setup:
        fp=os.path.join(d,fname)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(fp), exist_ok=True)
        if isinstance(content, bytes):
            open(fp,"wb").write(content)
        else:
            open(fp,"w").write(content)
    if setup_fn:
        setup_fn(d)
    o1,e1,c1=run_orig(*(args+[d]))
    o2,e2,c2=run_new(*(args+[d]))
    ok=(o1==o2 and e1==e2 and c1==c2)
    print(f"{name}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    if not ok:
        if o1!=o2:
            for i,(a,b) in enumerate(zip(o1.split("\n"), o2.split("\n"))):
                if a!=b:
                    print(f" {i} orig:{repr(a)[:200]}")
                    print(f" {i} new :{repr(b)[:200]}")
                    break
            if len(o1.split("\n"))!=len(o2.split("\n")):
                print(f" len {len(o1.split(chr(10)))} vs {len(o2.split(chr(10)))}")
        if e1!=e2:
            print(f" stderr {repr(e1[:300])} vs {repr(e2[:300])}")
    return ok

# More tests
test("gitignore", [("a.go","x\n"),(".gitignore","a.go\n")], [])
